column1: # Bound the Stonegate rescue cinematic's pacing on both sides, so the beats
# `blackthorn.md` Section 7 leaves untimed can be quoted with numbers.
# `cleak/u5-engine#38` closed the part of this that was a defect - the
# cinematic used to render nothing at all - and left the rest: two whole
# viewport rectangle dissolves and three 256-pixel cell reveals are still
# unmodelled. Section 7 publishes the dissolves as "roughly 8 to 14 s" and
# flags that figure **unverified**, and publishes the reveals as "31
# checkpoints" of one world tick rather than as a duration. Neither is a
# number an implementation can be written from.
# So measure them. Both sides step onto the trapdoor at the same moment and
# both are shot every four seconds. The reading wanted is which sample first
# shows each narration beat on each side; the gap between the two columns is
# the unmodelled time.
# Result, measured 2026-09-18. Each cell is the window's last non-blank row.
#   sample   stock                 engine
#   t04-t24  A TRAPDOOR!           A TRAPDOOR!
#   t28      refuge.               is disturbed!
#   t32-t36  is disturbed!         is disturbed!
#   t40      is disturbed!         my reach!"
#   t44      AVENTARI"             my reach!"
#   t48-t64  my reach!"            my reach!"
# Two gaps, one sample each, and both sides agree either side of them:
# 1. The trapdoor hold matches exactly - both hold `A TRAPDOOR!` through t24,
#    so `STONEGATE_TRAPDOOR_DEATH_HOLD_BIOS_TICKS` is right.
# 2. This engine reaches the slumber beat one sample before the original.
#    That is Section 7 step 2: "print the unending-darkness beat, then
#    dissolve the map viewport out to black", which runs before the refuge
#    fragments.
# 3. It then reaches the verdict two samples before the original, so a second
#    sample's worth is lost between the slumber beat and the verdict. That is
#    step 4's "three cell reveals" - the paired flash and the audio-envelope
#    sequence around them are already modelled.
# So each unmodelled hold is about one sample, not the "roughly 8 to 14 s"
# Section 6.3 gives for a dissolve and flags unverified. Read the bracket in
# samples rather than milliseconds: the nominal 4000 ms step is not wall clock,
# because every beat also pays for two screenshots.
# The roster panel is a lottery on this scenario. The fall runs
# `town-mode.md`'s shared mass-damage pass - one `1..8` roll per member - and
# the two sides never share a seed, so the `Avatar` HP row parts company on
# the fall and stays parted until the deaths land. Measured 2026-09-18: the
# original rolled 7 and this engine 5. A panel-only difference on that row has
# measured the roll, not the engine, and must be re-run before it means
# anything.
# What the panel *does* pin here is the timing, and that is not a lottery: the
# row must show a damaged living member for the whole sweep and turn to `0D`
# only after it. See the trapdoor arm of `apply_town_underfoot_effects`.
# **It is now a comparison, and it passes.** Measured 2026-09-18 after the
# holds below and the `A TRAPDOOR!` framing landed: all seventeen samples
# agree row for row, so the whole rescue - death sweep, three refuge
# fragments, shout, thunder, verdict and the acknowledgement cursor - tracks
# the original across a full minute. It was declared `not-a-comparison` while
# it was a measurement; that declaration is withdrawn rather than left to
# excuse a scenario that no longer needs excusing.
# Closed 2026-09-18. Bracketed over four runs at 15, 30, 45 and 60 ticks for
# each hold; 60 puts every one of the seventeen samples on the same narration
# beat as the original, and the three smaller values each leave the engine one
# or two beats ahead. `BLACKTHORN_RESCUE_WAIT_VIEWPORT_DISSOLVE` and
# `BLACKTHORN_RESCUE_WAIT_CELL_REVEALS` carry the figure.
# Read the *beats*, not the last row of the window. A scrolling window's last
# non-blank row is not a monotonic progress marker - it moves backwards when
# the window scrolls - and reading it that way made the 30-tick and 45-tick
# runs look like noise when they were in fact ordered.
# What is left after the pacing is row accounting, and one row of it is
# `cleak/u5-spec#279`: through t24 the original keeps a blank row under
# `A TRAPDOOR!` and this engine does not, which is that issue's question
# exactly. The samples from t48 read `offset+2` the other way.
# requires-seed: the party inside Stonegate, standing in the trapdoor ring's centre cell
